video_goal: Demonstrate the physical steps to configure a Nikon D850 camera for portrait photography, focusing on exposure and autofocus settings.
required_subjects_and_props: Nikon D850 camera body, 85mm portrait lens, a human subject (model) for the final focus check.

outline_steps.visual_action: Align the white dot on the base of an 85mm portrait lens with the white dot on the Nikon D850 lens mount, then twist the lens counter-clockwise until it audibly clicks into place.
Flick the power switch collar surrounding the shutter button on the top right of the camera body to the 'ON' position.
Press and hold the 'MODE' button on the top-left dial cluster while rotating the rear main command dial with the thumb until the letter 'M' appears on the top LCD screen.
Rotate the front sub-command dial with the index finger; the aperture value on the top LCD screen changes rapidly until it stops at 'f/1.8'.
Rotate the rear main command dial with the thumb; the shutter speed value on the top LCD screen changes until it reads '200'.
Press the 'ISO' button located just behind the shutter button and rotate the rear dial until the number '100' is displayed on the top LCD screen.
Press and hold the AF-mode button located on the lower-left front of the D850 body, right next to the lens mount.
While holding the AF-mode button, rotate the rear main command dial until the text 'AF-S' appears on the top LCD screen.
Still holding the AF-mode button, rotate the front sub-command dial until a single small square icon (Single-point AF) appears on the top LCD screen.
Press the 'Lv' (Live View) button located on the back right of the camera body to activate the large rear LCD screen, revealing a live feed of a portrait model.
Tap the rear touchscreen directly over the model's right eye; a small red focus box instantly moves to that exact spot on the screen.
Half-press the shutter button with the index finger; the red focus box on the rear LCD screen turns green, accompanied by a brief visual confirmation of sharp focus on the model's eye.
